name: Creamy Cajun Orzo Pasta with Butternut Squash, Mushrooms & Bell Peppers (Prep-Ahead)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe utilizes 4 medium food storage containers.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 small butternut squash
454 g cremini mushrooms
1 small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley

instructions.primary_message: Trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers. Transfer to a large baking sheet pan.
Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out the seeds, and small dice. Add to the baking sheet with the bell pepper.
Quarter mushrooms and add to the baking sheet. Drizzle veggies with oil, then sprinkle with Cajun seasoning and salt. Stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
4 tsp Cajun seasoning
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, stirring halfway through, until veggies soften, 12-15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 2-3 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
½ tsp garlic powder

instructions.primary_message: Add broth and orzo to the skillet with the onion, then stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid is mostly absorbed, about 10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 cups chicken or vegetable broth
283 g orzo pasta

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Set aside a small handful for serving.
Add roasted veggies, remaining parsley, and cream to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until thickened, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.

Divide orzo between storage containers, sprinkle with reserved parsley, and allow to cool completely, about 20 minutes. Once cool, cover containers and refrigerate. When ready to eat, heat orzo in a skillet, the oven, or a microwave and enjoy!
